newsitem.title: EGYPT: Militants kill three in southern Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Militants kill three in southern Egypt.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militants shot dead three people in a village in southern Egypt on Wednesday, security sources said.

They said gunmen opened fire at a cafe in the village of Tanda, near Mallawi town, about 260 km (160 miles) south of Cairo, killing retired police auxiliary Abdelbadea Mohammed Goma'a, 65, and farmer Samir el-Sayyed Taha, 45.

The gunmen ran off with Taha's unlicensed gun, which security sources said he used in joint patrols with police in the area. Civilians have been helping police hunt down militants who are waging a low-level guerrilla war in southern Egypt.
The militants shot dead police auxiliary Fattouh Abdelazeem Ahmed, 35, when he tried to apprehend them in a marketplace near the cafe, the sources said.

Police in Tanda believe the men were members of the militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), which in 1992 launched a bloody campaign to overthrow the government and turn Egypt into a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people, mainly policemen and militants, have been killed in political violence in Egypt since then.
